case_title: Vijender Kumar @ Vijay v. State of Delhi
aggravating_circumstances: Taking undue advantage of position, causing injury to an unarmed young boy
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 and sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Murder under Section 302 of the IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the son of a bus operator, suspected the deceased of misappropriating bus fare. During an argument at a bus terminal, the accused subjected the deceased to a personal search, recovered money, and became furious. He then retrieved a knife from his scooter and stabbed the deceased in the abdomen. The deceased was taken to a hospital where he later died. The trial court convicted the accused of murder based on circumstantial evidence, and the High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, finding that the incident did not meet the criteria for Exception 4 to Section 300 of the IPC.
